relevance_note: Retrospective pediatric Evans syndrome cohort in which whole-exome sequencing found a TNFAIP3 VUS in one child: "In one child, a heterozygous missense variant in the TNFAIP3 gene (c.1733C>T; p.Ser578Phe) was identified."
method_note: Read the whole paper manually; a short Python script assembled the JSON from values I chose, with Table 1 rows copied verbatim and checked against the table; all spans were then checked verbatim by script. Table 1 has patients as rows; labels 'Patient 1'-'Patient 6' are built from the table's 'Patient' column numbers (the paper prints only the numbers). All six cohort patients are included per the cohort-table rule, but only Patient 3 carries a TNFAIP3 variant; Patients 1-2 had negative WES and Patients 4-6 had no WES. Patient 3 is identified as the child with the TNFAIP3 variant because she is the only Table 1 row with 'TNFAIP3 VUS'; 'the mother' (variant carrier, asymptomatic) and 'the father' (variant absent) are her trio-tested parents, labeled by the paper's words. Results-text items given as '(n = 1)' were attached to the unique Table 1 patient with that manifestation (suspected autoimmune hepatitis/anti-LKM1/transaminases -> Patient 1; follicular hyperplasia -> Patient 2; recurrent aphthous stomatitis -> Patient 5; warm AIHA then ITP four years later -> Patient 4, the only AIHA-first patient). Group-inferred observed rows: AIHA after ITP for Patients 1-3 ('ITP preceded AIHA in three patients'; these are the only patients whose first cytopenia was ITP alone, the other two being the evolving multilineage cases 5-6); anti-HNA antibodies for Patients 2, 5, 6 (the three AIN-positive patients, 'in all three'). Age at onset = Table 1 'Age at First Cytopenia' (years per Table 2 header); one unnamed patient had an IM before first cytopenia, so for that patient overall onset may be earlier. Conservative choices: no checklist exclusions were derived from Table 1's per-patient IM lists or 'IM > 1 = No', nor from Patient 6's 'None' or the mother's 'clinically asymptomatic, with no history of autoimmune or autoinflammatory disease' (recorded only in phenotypic_features); ILD left not reported for Patient 2 despite 'HRCT normal'; sacroiliitis counted as 'arthritis or arthralgia' observed; mother's zygosity/inheritance left not reported (not stated for her); infections, family history and double-negative T cells are not attributable to individuals and were not recorded; country left not reported (only the center's location in Greece is stated). Contradictions/tensions: Table 1 lists 'autoimmune hepatitis' for Patient 1 while the Results call it 'suspected autoimmune hepatitis' (recorded observed with detail 'suspected'); Patients 5 and 6 are listed with no hemolysis at first cytopenia although ES requires AIHA and the text says DAT positivity preceded 'overt hemolysis or sustained thrombocytopenia', so the hemolysis exclusions may be time-limited; Patient 2's lymphadenopathy is 'transient' although the Methods define lymphoproliferative IM as persistent.
